overview: Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites predominantly in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, the U.K., Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand, with 939 warehouses worldwide as of August 30, 2026 [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, line L000734]. Its business model centers on providing a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products at low prices through a membership format, driving high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover that yields operational efficiency [10-K L000737]. The company sources merchandise primarily from direct suppliers, routing goods through cross-docking depots for efficient distribution to warehouses, with e-commerce operations integrated into this supply system [10-K L000738-L000741]. Average warehouse space is approximately 148,000 square feet, designed for merchandising efficiency and inventory control, operating under a no-frills, self-service structure to limit overhead costs [10-K L000742]. Membership fees, including $65 annual base fees in the U.S., contribute to revenues and include Executive memberships with rewards incentives [10-K L000773-L000782]. In 2026, Costco's merchandise offerings span core categories of foods and sundries, non-foods, fresh foods, warehouse ancillary services such as gasoline and pharmacy, and complementary businesses like e-commerce and travel [10-K L000746-L000763].
market_positioning_and_growth_outlook: Costco differentiates competitively through its membership warehouse format focusing on low prices supported by high volumes and inventory turnover, controlled selection of fast-moving SKUs (less than 4,000 per warehouse), and efficient, streamlined warehouse design [10-K L000737, L000744]. The membership renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026, indicating strong customer loyalty [10-K L000783]. Executive memberships accounted for approximately 42,300 thousand paid members in 2026 and drove about 75.2% of worldwide net sales [10-K L000782]. The company operated 939 warehouses globally, with 647 in the U.S. and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, and others across multiple international markets, reflecting broad geographic diversification [EX-99.1 L000021]. Catalysts for growth include warehouse expansion in existing and new markets, with attention to navigating local regulatory and competitive environments [10-K L000838-L000841].
future_developments_and_strategic_recomm: Costco plans to continue opening warehouses both in existing markets to increase share and in new markets where brand recognition and member acquisition present challenges [10-K L000838-L000841]. The company also pursues diversification and expansion of its supply chain, including expanding in-country production and private-label merchandise, to enhance control over merchandise and value [10-K L000768]. Monitoring the risks related to geographic concentration, especially U.S. and Canadian operations which represented 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income respectively in 2026, is critical for strategic decisions [10-K L000836-L000837]. Investments in e-commerce and warehouse ancillary services should continue to support member convenience and attract frequent shopping [10-K L000767].
insight: Insight: Costco's California operations alone comprised 26% of U.S. net sales in 2026, underscoring a significant geographic concentration risk that could materially affect overall financial performance if that market experiences downturns [10-K L000837].
